scene: AUTHORED EPILOGUE CODA, third person past, inline after '...and pulled the Commander close anyway, every time.' After the war Elyanka stayed in Drezen, mortal, useful and furious about it, keeping the dead-house by the south gate and the hearse in its yard and her Lady's appetites, all of them. When the Commander came she wrinkled her nose at the smell of warm living skin, every time, and pulled the Commander close anyway. This paragraph is one such visit told as a return, not a first night: boastful passion, contempt for warm flesh while wanting it, her claim on the Commander's eventual corpse spoken as an endearment, and nothing written down. The dead of the dead-house are scenery and never touched. Only Elyanka and the Commander.
